title: 140 intraday setups through 6 paper trading accounts + a 2-year backtest pipeline. Looking to trade simple setup ideas!
author: Enzobevmax
selftext:
Hey all. I’ve been building an intraday system and I’m find that outside setup ideas would help a lot more than more of my own tinkering. The following is an AI summary I had made showing what has been done so far. I'll mark my comments as "NAI" or non-AI" Happy to share our setup list with anyone who wants to trade ideas. Also open to any feedback. Bash away!

  
What it is  
  
Rule-based intraday trading of US stocks and ETFs. Flat by 15:55 ET, nothing held overnight.  
Entries are on 5-minute bar closes between 09:50 and 15:00 ET.  
Risk unit (R) = 0.25 × the stock’s daily ATR. Results are measured in R after costs.  
About 1,200 liquid names on SIP 1-minute data, executed through Alpaca.  
Everything is paper for now(NAI - Yes, I know the fills are instant if price touches). Real money waits until the main account shows a consistent record.  
I built it with an AI coding assistant doing the heavy lifting; I make the calls on what gets promoted or dropped.  
Accounts (6)  
  
Current Setup Allocation  
Primary: 14 setups. The best performers.  
Testing 1: 32 setups.  
Testing 2: 47 setups. Testing 1 and 2 hold promising candidates that need live proof.  
Setup Generator: 30 setups. Machine-generated, 10 new ones a night.  
Graveyard: 17 setups. Underperformers we keep running instead of deleting.  
Long-hold: one separate longer-term ETF account.  
That’s about 140 intraday setups live on paper, and a few hundred trades on a busy day.  
  
Backtesting (where most of the work goes)  
  
About 2 years of 1-minute data, roughly 500 sessions.  
A 4-month block is locked away as a one-shot final holdout, never looked at.  
The rest is split into training (to end of 2025) and validation (2026). A setup has to hold up in both.  
Costs are always in: 1 bp + $0.01/share each way, plus $0.02/share extra on stops.  
Every configuration tried is counted, and the pass bar gets stricter the more we try (t ≥ max(1.5, √(2 ln N))).  
Setups must beat random entries at the same time of day.  
A recent swarm of 200 dip-buying variants had zero pass. Most ideas die here, and we report the failures too.  
The generator screens about 3,000 rule combinations a night and keeps the top 10.  
Live side  
  
Setups move between accounts on their live record: trades, win rate vs. break-even win rate, avg R, and a t-stat.  
Avg R per trade beats win rate as the deciding number.  
Risk rules learned the hard way:  
A setup that’s down 2R on the day stops for the day.  
Two versions of the same setup can’t both hold the same stock.  
Bank half, protect the rest.  
Next up: replaying recorded past sessions through the live code, so new setups get \~50 “live” sessions before they ever trade.  
Honest status: some setups look genuinely good live, but nothing has cleared the full statistical bar yet. The main account isn’t consistently green, and paper fills are optimistic.  
  
What I’m after  
  
Intraday setups you’ve seen work or fail, especially longs that don’t just ride up days and shorts that survive up days.(NAI - My SHORTS are crushing on bad market days and neutral on up days, my LONGS skew slightly high on good market days and drop on bad market days, hence the need for more quality longs.)  
How you handle setups that only work in one market direction or condition.  
Ideas on data, fill modeling or validation.  
In return: our setup list in plain English (the rules, backtest numbers after costs, and live record so far), failures included. Comment or DM.  
  
Not financial advice. Just a nerd project comparing notes. Not great with screenshots and pictures on reddit but for further questions, I'll do my best to answer with pictures or AI feedback.  
  
TL;DR: Paper-trading 140 rule-based intraday stock setups across five Alpaca accounts, backtested on two years of minute data; trying to swap setups.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
10 machine-made setups a night is the slippery bit. with 140 running, some look great in Testing 1 by luck, so promoting the best performers promotes the lucky ones unless the bar rises with how many you test.

catching that is why Quantradin exists, I built it to give each rule a live, shadow or shelf verdict first. quantradin.com

how many trades before a setup leaves Testing 1?

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body:
The basis for the setup generator is that its an additional input tool I thought of that's minimal cost and could either offer genuine setups to run OR to run variants off of those setups since testing is so cheap. 

I've found that even some setups that were backtested with non-live trading made significant strides in the other direction when live-tested. 

Just wanted a way to more ideas since live testing with paper is so easy with this setup. We can also tear apart or build up certain areas of setups leading to new potentially viable setups we otherwise wouldn't have thought of.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: cheap testing is exactly why the variants pile up though. if the generator throws out ten cousins of one setup and one of them wins, a good part of that win is just the cost of trying ten. I'd write down how many siblings a winner had before it goes live.

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body:
Definitely understand your logic and its the correct mindset for sure but the generator creates the setup automatically, automatically then backtests it through the two years of data for potential viability, then delivers it for live testing. So yes, it could be on of 10 similar ones but traits from the bad ones caused those to not make the cut, giving us a slightly more polished product. 

Gotta say though, there is still minimal optimism for the generator. It's only been on for a few days and our 100-ish other live setups have all come from other sources, not randomly generated. 

Love the help though!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fair, cutting on traits from the losers does help. I'd still keep the generator's setups as their own bucket for a month next to the 100 from other sources, so you can see whether it's earning its spot.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Good setup, and the images make it clearer. One thing I noticed is that the top setups show +10 to +15 R each, but the account tiles are all down since start (Primary about -$2,182, Testing 2 about -$3,426). That gap is worth chasing down: it could be costs, stops filling worse than assumed, or overlapping setups holding the same stocks. With 140 setups, some will show a t-stat near 3 by luck, since your own bar for that many tries is about 3.1, and these have only 7 or 8 sessions each. On long setups that only work on up days, I'd split results by market regime, defined before testing. Full disclosure, I work at Cymetica, so one idea source might be our Event Cards, which turn a news event into a basket of related stocks with a sourced report and a paper balance to try it on.

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body:
Thank you. It should be clear, as with all of our projects like this, that it's a work in progress and I'm not suggesting any of this is the correct way.

As much as it sounds like an excuse, the bulk of those draw downs are from the beginning of the creation of those accounts and losses since their inceptions. I have made minimal efforts to work with position sizing as it's all paper and I have been more concerned with win rate, ave R return, break-even win rate, etc.

Funny - I just added a market regime-esque column on my setup leaderboard last night to start tracking what type of market offers the most success with that particular setup so you are spot on!

Really really appreciate the event card idea. I've toyed with earnings reports and news supporting stock focus but I have not made great efforts to put any focus here. The goal was to use news as an "extra layer" indicator to play a stock or not but again, I have not moved forward with that. I do have a hard rule now to not trade tickers two days before/after earnings to eliminate some bias.

Thank you for this!

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Thanks, and good that the regime column is already in. One idea on the earnings rule: besides excluding the two days around earnings, you could tag those trades and track them as their own group, so you can see if news-related trades behave differently instead of just avoiding them. Event Cards keep a news event tied to a basket with a sourced report, so you can use it as a reference for the "extra layer" idea. Good luck with the build.

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body: I like that, and it's really no extra cost or effort for me. I never max out my Claude usage so I am always trying to find things to add. With those suggestions too, it will help to start tracking now, even if I don't explore it until much further down the road - just more data.
